external_entities.name: other teams' backends
external_entities.description: Backends belonging to other teams that call the inference gateway.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Other teams' backends call our inference gateway
external_entities.notes: Two of the calling services are in a different cloud.

external_entities.name: ML engineers
external_entities.description: People who publish new model artifacts to the model registry bucket.
external_entities.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket
external_entities.notes: The source is unsure what governs who can push and thinks it is a shared group account.

processes.name: inference gateway
processes.description: A FastAPI service on GKE that receives inference requests and forwards them to the model server. It is exposed on the internet and writes requests and responses to the inference log.
processes.source_excerpt: our inference gateway, a FastAPI service on GKE that we expose on the internet
processes.notes: Callers pass an API key in a header. Keys are issued per calling team and have never been expired.

processes.name: model server
processes.description: The server that runs the actual model on GPU nodes and loads model artifacts at startup.
processes.source_excerpt: the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes in our model network
processes.notes: There is no authentication between the gateway and the model server.

data_stores.name: model registry bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket from which the model server loads model artifacts at startup and to which ML engineers publish new model artifacts.
data_stores.notes: The source says the bucket is trusted and does not believe anything verifies that an artifact has not been swapped.

data_stores.name: Redis feature store
data_stores.description: A Redis store containing customer features such as account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Redis feature store on the same network. ... The features include account age and spend bands per customer.
data_stores.notes: Redis has no password and is only reachable inside the model network.

data_stores.name: inference log
data_stores.description: A BigQuery log containing every request and response for debugging, including raw prompts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery
data_stores.notes: The log contains raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

data_flows.name: inference requests
data_flows.description: Inference requests sent by other teams' backends to the inference gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Callers pass an API key in a header.
data_flows.notes: The API key is passed in a header. Keys are issued per calling team and have never been expired.

data_flows.name: forwarded requests
data_flows.description: The inference gateway forwards requests to the model server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway forwards the request to the model server
data_flows.notes: There is no authentication between the gateway and the model server.

data_flows.name: model artifact loads
data_flows.description: The model server loads model artifacts from the model registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.
data_flows.notes: The model server uses its own service account for this. The source says it trusts the bucket and does not believe artifact swapping is verified.

data_flows.name: customer feature reads
data_flows.description: The model server reads customer features from the Redis feature store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the model server reads from a Redis feature store on the same network
data_flows.notes: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.
data_flows.data_description: Customer features including account age and spend bands per customer

data_flows.name: request and response logging
data_flows.description: The inference gateway writes every request and response to the inference log for debugging.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging.
data_flows.notes: The logged data includes raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.
data_flows.data_description: Every request and response, including raw prompts

data_flows.name: model artifact publication
data_flows.description: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the model registry bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source is unsure what governs who can push and thinks it is a shared group account.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone from which calling services reach the exposed inference gateway.
trust_boundaries.notes: Two calling services are in a different cloud.

trust_boundaries.name: model network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the model server and Redis feature store.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: GPU nodes in our model network
trust_boundaries.notes: The model network is meant to be reachable only from the gateway; Redis is only reachable inside the model network.

trust_boundaries.name: internal
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation-controlled zone for components whose specific network location is not stated.
trust_boundaries.notes: The source does not state the network location of the model registry bucket or BigQuery inference log.

assumptions.assumption: The inference gateway presents a web interface because it is described as a FastAPI service.
assumptions.basis: FastAPI is a web service framework, and the text describes the gateway as a FastAPI service.

assumptions.assumption: The model registry bucket contains business-critical model artifacts.
assumptions.basis: The bucket stores model artifacts used by the model server and receives newly published model artifacts.

assumptions.assumption: The Redis feature store contains personally identifiable information.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents are customer-specific features, including account age and spend bands per customer.

assumptions.assumption: The Redis feature store is confidential.
assumptions.basis: Its stated contents are customer-specific account age and spend-band features, whose disclosure can harm or identify customers.

assumptions.assumption: The model artifacts are business-critical data in the publication flow.
assumptions.basis: The flow publishes model artifacts used by the model server.
